Chapter format

Every chapter is one directory with three reader-facing documents, one grader, and one reference solution. The three documents answer three different questions and are read at three different times; merging any two of them produces a page that is simultaneously too long to work from and too thin to learn from.

chapters/NN-slug/
  README.md      one-screen index: goal, time, difficulty, edit list, doc links
  overview.md    how the mechanism works, in general. Concept + diagrams.
  problem.md     what you must build, what exactly is graded, and the hints.
  example.md     a complete, annotated implementation. Implementation-heavy.
  checks/        Go test suite — the only thing that defines "done"
reference/chNN/  reference implementation, cumulative, separate Go module

The three documents

overview.mdproblem.mdexample.md
Questionhow does this work?what must I do?what does a full one look like?
Read whenbefore you startat the keyboardafter a real attempt
Shapeprose, diagrams, worked byte-level examplestables, claims, hintscode, diffs, annotations
Lengthlong, discursiveshort, scannableas long as the code
Spoilersnone — concept onlynonetotal, by design
Ends withself-check questionsdone-whencomparison checklist

The rule that keeps them honest: overview.md may not contain a working implementation, and example.md may not contain new concepts. If an idea only appears in the example, it belongs in the overview first.

overview.md — the general doc

Free-form, but must contain:

  1. Why it exists — the mechanism in the domain's terms, not Go's.
  2. A diagram — mermaid for GitHub/HTML, plus a short ASCII version when the

diagram is load-bearing, because the terminal cannot render mermaid.

  1. Real bytes — an actual SSE chunk, an actual JSON body, an actual file.

Not "the model returns chunks"; the chunk.

  1. A failure map — the ways this goes wrong, drawn as a tree, each branch

labelled with the case id that catches it. This is the link between teaching and grading.

  1. Where the real implementations go further — pi/crush/PiG file paths, and

what they add that we skipped.

  1. Self-check — 3–5 questions answerable only if the concept landed, each

pointing at the section that answers it.

problem.md — the contract

Fixed sections, in this order. No freestyle.

  1. Your task — one sentence, naming a capability, never a function.
  2. The contract — the signature, the wire shape, the file format. Tables.
  3. What the verifier does — what it runs, and that it inspects requests,

not only output.

  1. The verifier will assert that — one bullet per graded case, phrased as a

promise, named by case id. Must match checks/ exactly; if they diverge the checks are truth and this page is a bug.

  1. Notes — edge cases you must handle; deliberate omissions with a link to

the real implementation; the output contract (stdout vs stderr, exit codes).

  1. Hints — three rungs, spoiler-collapsed, identical to internal/hints.
  2. Done when — kata submit NN green, plus one self-check sentence.

example.md — the implementation doc

The full annotated answer, structured as the thinking order, not the file order:

  1. The shape — the function split, before any code.
  2. Steps — one section per decision, each with the code and why.
  3. The diffs — wrong vs right for each trap, labelled with the case id.
  4. The complete file — or a pointer to reference/chNN/.
  5. Production delta — a table of what pi/crush add and why we skipped it.
  6. Comparison checklist — differences that are bugs vs differences that are

style.

Which driver

Each case names its driver, and the chapter's problem.md groups the claims by it. The rule is in architecture.md: black box by default, function level only for pure transforms with awkward inputs.

// black box: build and run ./agent/cmd/agent
res := blackbox.Run(t, env(srv.BaseURL()), "-p", "list the files")

// function level: a pinned, deliberately small surface
got := agent.SubstituteArgs("Deploy to $0 in $1", []string{"staging", "eu"})

A case that pins a function must say so in problem.md under "given surface", so a learner never discovers the requirement from a compile error.

The build tag

Chapter checks carry //go:build kata_checks. That keeps go test ./... green in a fresh clone, where agent/ is still the starter and every case is supposed to fail. kata submit and kata verify add the tag themselves, so you never pass it by hand.

go test -tags=kata_checks ./chapters/01-chat-with-the-model/checks/

Indexing

CodeCrafters indexes stages globally with sections as headers. We do not: a chapter is the unit, NN is its identity, and cases inside a chapter are addressable only by case id (for hints). Inserting a chapter never renumbers a learner's progress, and the arc stays editable while it is being written.

Grouping into parts

PartChaptersThe leap
I. Wire01–02talk to a model, survive its output
II. Act03–04tools, then the loop that drives them
III. Remember05–07prompt, sessions, budget
IV. Extend08–09steering, skills
V. Compose10–11subagents, MCP

Part boundaries are where the mental model changes, and where a learner can stop and still have something useful.
